Reports from three customer-facing teams, all about things turning up where they should not.

1. Support: a customer found a label on one of their issues that carries another customer's project name; nobody in their workspace created it. The label picker had been sent a stale set of label ids.
2. Support: an issue was created as a sub-issue of an issue that belongs to a different workspace, another one under an issue from a different project of the same workspace, and a third under an issue that had been archived. None of these parents can be seen from where the sub-issues live.
3. Support: a reply "vanished": it had been posted as a reply to a comment on a different issue, and another one as a reply to a comment that had already been deleted, so neither shows in any thread.
4. Security: an issue was assigned to a person who is not a member of the workspace (they received the assignment email), a project was created with a stranger as its lead, and someone who had left the workspace was @-mentioned through the composer's suggestions and got notified.

Expected behaviour. Everything a change points at must be usable from the workspace the change is made in. An assignee or a project lead must be a current member of that workspace. Labels must be that workspace's own labels, and an issue never shows a label that is not, whatever was attached to it before. A parent issue must be a live issue of the same project. A reply must be to a live, top-level comment on the same issue. People mentioned in a comment, whether written as @handles or supplied by the composer, are only ever current members of the workspace: mentions of anyone else are ignored, not refused, and never notified. A reference to something that belongs to another workspace is refused the same way as any other cross-workspace access. A reference that does not exist, is archived or deleted, is not a current member, is a parent from a different project, or is a reply to a reply is refused as not found. A refused change changes nothing: no issue or comment is created, no field or label is changed, and nothing is announced.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. 93	function issueFilters(input: IssueFilterInput): readonly SQL[] {
94	  const scope: ArchiveScope = shouldFilterArchived(input)
95	    ? {}
96	    : { includeArchived: true };
97	
98	  return compact(
99	    orgPredicate(issues.orgId, input.orgId),
100	    livePredicate(issues.archivedAt, scope),
101	    input.projectId === undefined
102	      ? undefined
103	      : eq(issues.projectId, input.projectId),
104	    input.status === undefined || input.status.length === 0
105	      ? undefined
106	      : inArray(issues.status, [...input.status]),
107	    input.priority === undefined || input.priority.length === 0
108	      ? undefined
109	      : inArray(issues.priority, [...input.priority]),
110	    input.assigneeId === undefined
111	      ? undefined
112	      : input.assigneeId === null
113	        ? isNull(issues.assigneeId)
114	        : eq(issues.assigneeId, input.assigneeId),
115	    input.authorId === undefined
116	      ? undefined
117	      : eq(issues.authorId, input.authorId),
118	    input.dueBefore === undefined ? undefined : lt(issues.dueAt, input.dueBefore),
119	    input.query === undefined
120	      ? undefined
121	      : or(
122	          like(issues.title, `%${input.query}%`),
123	          like(issues.description, `%${input.query}%`),
124	        ),
125	    input.labelIds === undefined || input.labelIds.length === 0
126	      ? undefined
127	      : inArray(
128	          issues.id,
129	          getDb()
130	            .select({ id: issueLabels.issueId })
131	            .from(issueLabels)
132	            .where(
133	              and(
134	                orgPredicate(issueLabels.orgId, input.orgId),
135	                inArray(issueLabels.labelId, [...input.labelIds]),
136	              ),
137	            ),
138	        ),
139	  );

142	export async function listIssues(
143	  input: IssueFilterInput,
144	): Promise<Page<Issue>> {
145	  const db = getDb();
146	  const filters = issueFilters(input);
147	  const sort = { sortColumn: issues.createdAt, idColumn: issues.id };
148	
149	  const total = db
150	    .select({ value: count() })
151	    .from(issues)
152	    .where(and(...filters))
153	    .get();
154	
155	  const rows = db
156	    .select()
157	    .from(issues)
158	    .where(and(...filters, ...compact(keysetPredicate(sort, input.cursor))))
159	    .orderBy(desc(issues.createdAt), desc(issues.id))
160	    .limit(probeLimit(input.limit))
161	    .all();
162	
163	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(
164	    input.orgId,
165	    rows.map((row) => row.id as IssueId),
166	  );
167	
168	  return toPage(
169	    rows,
170	    input.limit,
171	    total?.value ?? 0,
172	    (row) => toIssue(row, (labels[row.id] ?? []).map((label) => label.id)),
173	    (row) => ({ id: row.id, sortValue: row.createdAt }),
174	  );
175	}

178	 * The list view needs comment and attachment counts per row. Two grouped
179	 * queries beat N+1 round trips, so the counts are folded in afterwards.

181	export async function listIssuesWithRelations(
182	  input: IssueFilterInput,
183	): Promise<Page<IssueWithRelations>> {
184	  const db = getDb();
185	  const page = await listIssues(input);
186	  const ids = page.items.map((issue) => issue.id);
187	  if (ids.length === 0) {
188	    return { items: [], nextCursor: page.nextCursor, total: page.total };
189	  }
190	
191	  const commentCounts = db
192	    .select({ issueId: comments.issueId, value: count() })
193	    .from(comments)
194	    .where(
195	      and(
196	        orgPredicate(comments.orgId, input.orgId),
197	        inArray(comments.issueId, [...ids]),
198	        isNull(comments.archivedAt),
199	      ),
200	    )
201	    .groupBy(comments.issueId)
202	    .all();
203	
204	  const attachmentCounts = db
205	    .select({ issueId: attachments.issueId, value: count() })
206	    .from(attachments)
207	    .where(
208	      and(
209	        orgPredicate(attachments.orgId, input.orgId),
210	        inArray(attachments.issueId, [...ids]),
211	      ),
212	    )
213	    .groupBy(attachments.issueId)
214	    .all();
215	
216	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(input.orgId, ids);
217	  const commentsBy = new Map(commentCounts.map((r) => [r.issueId, r.value]));
218	  const attachmentsBy = new Map(
219	    attachmentCounts.map((r) => [r.issueId, r.value]),
220	  );
221	
222	  return {
223	    items: page.items.map((issue) => ({
224	      issue,
225	      labels: labels[issue.id] ?? [],
226	      commentCount: commentsBy.get(issue.id) ?? 0,
227	      attachmentCount: attachmentsBy.get(issue.id) ?? 0,
228	    })),
229	    nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
230	    total: page.total,
231	  };
232	}

356	    .update(issues)
357	    .set({
358	      ...(input.title === undefined ? {} : { title: input.title }),

406	  orgId: OrgId,
407	  issueId: IssueId,
408	  status: IssueStatus,
409	): Promise<Issue> {

411	  const current = getDb()
412	    .select()

content.text:
The fix is in place. Type-check, lint, and the full test suite (73 files, 617 tests) all pass. I also ran a temporary scenario file covering each refusal and removed it afterwards.

The changes:

- **Labels:** `listLabelsForIssues` now joins only labels from the issue's own workspace, so a foreign label never shows. Create and update refuse a label from another workspace as a tenant-scope violation, and a missing one as not found, before anything is written.
- **Parent issue:** must be live and in the same project. A parent from another workspace is a tenant-scope violation; anything else is not found.
- **Assignee and project lead:** must be a current member (live and `active`). Otherwise they are refused as not found, before the write or event.
- **Replies:** the target must be a live, top-level comment on the same issue. The check runs before the rate-limit charge.
